Shopkeeping Rules
Before You Start

You won a million in the lottery. The Republic took it, and all you got was the right to use this shop in the Upper Levels.

Luckily, someone is willing to help: Weight, the "Straight Arrow" who made it out of the Lower Levels. He lets you sell his goods and lent you money to open.

This guide covers four things: how Weight's consignment works, residence and taxes, the regulars, and where to find stock.
Weight's Consignment
Consigned goods
Weight delivers on days 2, 4 and 9, then once a week. The goods go into your shop for you to sell; their description says "Weight's consignment".
60/40 split
For anything sold at the counter, Weight takes 60% of the price and you keep 40%. Whatever does not sell stays with you.
The loan
The 1500 he lent you on day 1, plus the first week of rent he covered on day 4. Weight says there is no rush; nothing comes out of your share. Your 40% is all yours.
Settling Up

Weight starts each visit by settling last week:

· Sold at the counter: he takes 60%.
· Gone from the shop but not sold at the counter (sold elsewhere, used up): counted as sold at list price.
· Still in the shop: keep selling.

Then he drops off a new batch.

If you are short on cash, the rest waits until next time.
Residence and Taxes
Residence period
Counted from day 1, when the Republic official came. He comes back on day 7 and takes 30% of your cash as "support for the Republic".
Sixty days
Sixty days of residence without trouble, and you may buy a permanent Upper Levels residence permit. Get rid of any contraband early.
Support for the Republic
The Republic official will come back for money, based on the cash you hold, with no receipt. The more cash, the more they take.
Regulars

· Bruce: an old man who has lived in the Upper Levels for forty years and now works the recycling stations. Buy from him and he brings a batch every 3 days, 30% off. Help him and he will remember.

· The Helios butler: comes every 4 days to buy fresh food for the young lady. No cans. Pays well.

· Officer Dex: patrols this area. Report sellers carrying high-level contraband for a bounty based on what gets seized.
Where Stock Comes From

Upper Levels sellers will come to you:

· People moving out: household goods.
· The deli courier: freshly made food.
· The private doctor: medical supplies.
· Estate clerks, auction clerks, collectors, fallen aristocrats: luxuries.

Put luxuries in the display case to draw in wealthy shoppers. Their budget is roughly enough for the priciest piece on display.
A Few Tips

· The default price is a fair price. Upper Levels customers care about appearances.

· Keep some room in the shop. If Weight can't fit a delivery, he only leaves part of it.

· Haadasgen goes in the freezer; salads, sandwiches and cake go in the fridge. Left out overnight, they lose their value.

· Things people leave with you for safekeeping can't be sold. Don't lose them either.
